clue.text: Discharged from army, having received bomb injury in action

indicators.note: an injury damages and disorders things, so the word bomb is knocked out of shape
one word having received another holds it inside itself

blocks.note: a deed is an action
the letters of bomb rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier is invalided out of the army after being hurt by a bomb in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharged' could suggest firing a weapon, but here it is release from service; demob is British slang for demobilise.
explanation.definitionFit: Demob is the informal British term for releasing soldiers from military service, so demobbed means released from it.

clue.text: Straying on to railway when travelling in search of adventure

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on to another sits directly after it

blocks.note: errant means wandering or straying
RY is a standard abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone wanders onto the railway line while travelling around looking for excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Errantry is the roaming life of a knight-errant, who wandered the land seeking adventures and deeds of chivalry.

clue.text: Six or more balls into the bargain

blocks.note: first meaning, a cricket one: an over is six balls, and 'or more' adds something on top of it
second meaning: in addition, besides

explanation.surface: Someone throws in half a dozen or more balls as an extra in a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end, so six balls or more is an over and something above it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in addition to what is already counted, exactly as the phrase into the bargain does.

clue.text: Graduate digesting books on bird in Africa

indicators.note: something digesting food has taken it inside itself, so the graduate holds the rest

blocks.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books
a swan is a bird

explanation.surface: A university graduate reads books about a bird while in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply puts the books before the bird; OT for the Old Testament is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a landlocked country of southern Africa, so it is somewhere located in Africa.

clue.text: Collapse of girl coming out with torn lace

indicators.note: torn fabric is ripped apart, so the word lace is pulled into a new order

blocks.note: a deb, or debutante, is a girl coming out into society
the letters of lace rearranged

explanation.surface: A debutante's big night ends badly when her lace gown rips.
explanation.walkthrough: Coming out is the old society debut of a young woman, hence a deb.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, ignominious failure or breakdown, a synonym for a collapse.

clue.text: A great many copies of the notes?

blocks.note: first meaning: large numbers
second meaning: written music, the sheets that set down the notes for players

explanation.surface: Someone has printed a huge number of copies of their notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests lecture notes; the question mark hints they are musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so scores means very many; a musical score is the written copy of a composition.

clue.text: Scoundrel losing his head in church

indicators.note: losing a head means the first letter of the word is cut off

blocks.note: a knave is a dishonest rogue

explanation.surface: A villain is beheaded inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a place, the part found in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The nave is the main central body of a church building, where the congregation sits.

clue.text: Hypocrite's extremely effective support for husband in city

indicators.note: the husband sits in the city, held inside its name
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters only
in a down clue a support sits underneath, so this piece comes after the rest

blocks.note: Paris is a city
H is the abbreviation for husband
the first and last letters of effective

explanation.surface: A hypocrite gives very effective backing to a husband living in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees are portrayed in the Gospels as self-righteous, so the word has come to mean a sanctimonious, insincere person.

clue.text: Intrude, giving directions to vehicle crossing river

indicators.note: a vehicle crossing something goes over and around it, enclosing it

blocks.note: E and N, east and north, are compass directions
a coach is a vehicle
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A trespasser points the way to a bus as it crosses a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to advance gradually beyond proper limits onto another's ground, a synonym for intruding.

clue.text: Upright exactly in tune

blocks.note: first meaning: straight and level, as a wall that is plumb
second meaning: pitched accurately, as a note sung right

explanation.surface: An honest person who also sings perfectly in tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright' looks like moral honesty, which the answer also means, but here it is a builder's sense of vertical.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes something perfectly vertical or aligned, and a note at precisely the correct pitch.

clue.text: He provides courses in art — a sure 10, it turns out

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned over and come out differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the answer to clue 10 across

explanation.surface: Someone runs courses in art and is certain they are genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' suggests classes, but they are courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurateur owns and runs a restaurant, serving diners their starters, mains and desserts.

clue.text: Branch of maths more trying to confused characters

indicators.note: characters are letters, and confused ones are muddled up into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A schoolchild finds one area of mathematics more exasperating for muddled minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder; the characters are letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Trigonometry is the area of mathematics dealing with the angles and sides of triangles.

clue.text: Sounds like a fellow's article in verse

indicators.note: sounds like says the spoken form, not the spelling, is what counts

blocks.note: Stan is a fellow, and a is an article

explanation.surface: A man's piece of writing is in poetry form.
explanation.walkthrough: Stan stands for any man, and the indefinite article a follows his possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem, a verse in the sense of a poem's section.

clue.text: A great deal of corporal punishment

blocks.note: first meaning: plenty, a British informal sense
second meaning: beatings with a whip

explanation.surface: Someone receives a heavy dose of physical punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A great deal of' reads as a quantity of punishment; 'of' is just a link between two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Lashings is British slang for abundant amounts, and lashings are also strokes of a whip given as a beating.

clue.text: They may suit the retired Briton

definitions.text: They may suit the retired Briton

blocks.clueFragment: They may suit the retired Briton
blocks.note: surface reading: some things are well suited to an older British pensioner
setter's reading: a two-piece suit worn by someone who has retired to bed for the night

explanation.walkthrough: Retired means gone to bed, not stopped working, and 'suit' is the garment; the Briton spells the word the British way, with a y.
explanation.definitionFit: These are loose jacket-and-trouser nightclothes, a suit worn by someone who has gone to bed.

clue.text: Where to get a bite in a river in Palermo, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the city name is only one possible arrangement of its letters

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller asks where to grab a snack in a Sicilian city with a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where to get a bite' suggests a café; it is the mouth. The river goes into the mix with Palermo.
explanation.definitionFit: A premolar is a tooth between the canines and molars, one of the teeth that bite and chew food.

clue.text: Take up cryptaesthesia? Pointless

blocks.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is another name for cryptaesthesia
pointless means of no use, read as O (nothing) and USE

explanation.surface: A sceptic asks whether it is worth adopting a belief in the paranormal, and decides it is futile.
explanation.walkthrough: Pointless is read as 'no use', with O standing for no or nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to adopt or support it, which is what taking up a cause means.

clue.text: He may look and listen out around Tyneside

indicators.note: out suggests the word listen is put out of its usual order
the rearranged letters go around the other piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: Someone on Tyneside keeps watch and listens carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area around Newcastle in North East England, so it stands for NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a soldier or guard posted to keep watch, someone whose job is to look out.

clue.text: With beer on board, he is a traveller

indicators.note: on board means aboard a ship, so the beer sits inside the ship's abbreviation

blocks.note: SS, steamship, the vessel one is aboard
ale is beer
he, a male, is a man

explanation.surface: A passenger is drinking beer on a ship or plane.
explanation.walkthrough: On board conventionally means inside SS, the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling salesman goes from place to place selling goods, so traveller is the trade's old name for one.

clue.text: One fighting for a tool kept by Remus's brother

indicators.note: something kept by another is held inside it

blocks.note: Brer (brother) is how the Uncle Remus tales of Joel Chandler Harris name their animals, like Brer Rabbit
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes

explanation.surface: Someone fights to get a tool back from the brother of Remus, Romulus's twin.
explanation.walkthrough: Remus suggests the Roman twin Romulus, but it is Uncle Remus, whose stories call each character Brer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawler is someone who takes part in rough, noisy fights, especially in the street.

clue.text: Former songwriter selling abroad

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, one who sells abroad

blocks.note: ex means former
Cole Porter, the American songwriter

explanation.surface: A one-time composer of songs now sells them overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: An exporter is a firm or person sending goods to foreign countries for sale.

clue.text: VAT debtor catches a cold here

definitions.note: a place described, not a synonym

blocks.note: a tun is a large cask or vat

taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who owes value added tax ends up with a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT looks like the British sales tax but is a plain vat; capitals mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the treeless frozen plain of the Arctic, where the climate is bitterly cold.

clue.text: Pasta for the Head

blocks.note: first meaning: a ribbon of pasta
second meaning: informal word for one's head

explanation.surface: Someone serves spaghetti to the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Head suggests a headteacher; it is the head on one's shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is a strip of pasta, and noodle is also slang for the brain or the skull.

clue.text: In "Alice" he won with difficulty now and then

indicators.note: something done with difficulty is struggled over, so the letters are wrestled into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor in a production of Alice took the prize only after a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition setting the scene, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means occasionally or from time to time, the same idea as at intervals.

clue.text: We may get it in the neck in Munster

definitions.text: We may get it in the neck

blocks.clueFragment: We may get it in the neck

clue.text: In retrospect, a bit of an emotional book

explanation.surface: An heir apparent is fated to take to the skies.
explanation.definitionFit: Airborne describes an aircraft or bird once it is off the ground and in the air.

clue.text: Friend in band recovering from illness

indicators.note: the friend is placed in the band, inside its letters

blocks.note: a ring is a band

explanation.surface: A friend in a pop group is getting better after being ill.
